title: Fuel — Replacement of the Inner Tank Boost Pump Inlet Housings
abstract: Mandatory replacement of the four inner tank boost pump inlet housings by items with a continuous flange radius, required by airworthiness directive after a fatigue crack allowed fuel to leak into a dry bay.

sections.planning_reason: A fuel leak into the left inner dry bay was traced to a fatigue crack in the boost pump inlet housing flange radius at 26 900 flight cycles. Teardown of eight further housings returned from service found sub-critical indications in three. The crack initiates at a machining transition in the flange radius that carries a higher stress concentration than the original substantiation assumed. The ignition risk associated with a leak into the dry bay makes the finding safety significant, and the airworthiness authority has issued a directive requiring inspection and replacement.
sections.description: Each inlet housing is replaced by an item machined with a continuous radius and a shot-peened flange face. The obsolete valve kit MON278175-36 is removed and its function is taken by the restrictor NY844698-29, repositioned outboard of the flange so that its mounting no longer loads the radius. The upper sensor NYD659955-61 is retained and its harness is re-clipped clear of the new restrictor position. Anchor nuts EN968165-23 and swaged collars LN41340-8C are used at the revised flange joint.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Defuel the tank and purge it to the entry standard, and post a tank entry watch. Remove the wing tank access panels and enter the tank. Remove the boost pump using AMM-T-28-20-11-000-001-A. Remove the obsolete valve kit MON278175-36 and cap the port. Remove the inlet housing and do a fluorescent penetrant inspection of the mating structure at the flange land. Install the replacement housing, using anchor nuts EN968165-23 and swaged collars LN41340-8C at the flange joint, and torque to the values in the accomplishment instructions. Install the restrictor NY844698-29 at the outboard position and re-clip the harness of the sensor NYD659955-61 clear of it. Install the boost pump using AMM-T-28-20-11-400-001-A. Repeat for the remaining three positions. Close the tank, refuel and do a full leak check at operating pressure with the dry bay drains observed. Do a fuel system functional test. Record the embodiment and cancel the repetitive inspection.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to TITAN-88 aircraft up to and including MSN T00201. Aircraft from MSN T00203 onwards were built with the replacement housing and are outside the scope of this Service Bulletin. All four positions must be at the same standard before the repetitive inspection required by the directive may be cancelled; an aircraft with fewer than four positions converted stays on the inspection.
sections.material_note: Kit K2820-1030-01 covers one aircraft, four positions. Kit lead time is thirty-four weeks. Removed housings must be returned to Aeralis for the fleet monitoring programme and must not be scrapped locally, whatever their condition.

type_data.compliance_time: Within 36 months after the effective date of the airworthiness directive, with a repetitive detailed inspection at intervals of 3 000 flight cycles until accomplishment.
